1.support: The aim of this report is to describe six consequent patients with bilateral pneumonia and ARDS, who had excessively low respiratory system compliance and severe hypercapnia with severe respiratory acidosis.
1.location: Page 1, Introduction, last paragraph (also Abstract 'Purpose', page 1)

2.support: For patient enrolment, eligibility criteria had to be met within 24 hours of ICU admission or within 24 hours from commencing mechanical ventilation. Patients with any of the following were excluded from the study: known bronchial asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), previous lung or chest wall surgery...

3.support: Six consecutive patients with severe hypercapnia and a concomitant significant hypoxemia requiring moderate to high PEEP which was set according to the algorithm of ARDSnet guidelines were enrolled. All six patients had bilateral pneumonia with ARDS.

4.support: Six consecutive patients with severe hypercapnia and a concomitant significant hypoxemia requiring moderate to high PEEP which was set according to the algorithm of ARDSnet guidelines were enrolled.

5.support: There are a few limitations in this report. First is its size. However, it should be noticed that patients with severe ARDS and a concomitant severe respiratory acidosis to an extent reported in this small series are hard to come by.
5.location: Page 7, Discussion, limitations paragraph (no sample-size or power calculation appears anywhere in the report)

6.support: PEEP was adjusted according to end expiratory transpulmonary (EETP) pressure, with the aim of keeping EETP pressure close to zero or slightly positive...inspiratory driving pressure was adjusted according to end inspiratory transpulmonary (EITP) pressure, with the aim of achieving a tidal volume of 6-8 mL/kg (IBW), while at the same time not exceeding EITP pressure of 25 cm H2O.
6.location: Pages 2-3, Intervention section and Figure 1; success of delivery reported on page 3, Results ('In all patients esophageal balloon insertion was successful and without any complications')

7.support: All patients were monitored continuously with arterial line, heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, end tidal CO2, and transpulmonary thermodilution technique with continuous cardiac output assessment using arterial pulse contour analysis (PiCCO2).
7.location: Page 3, Intervention section (outcomes listed in Table 3, page 6)

8.support: No blinding or masking of outcome assessors is described; the esophageal balloon was inserted and PEEP and inspiratory driving pressure were titrated at the bedside by the treating team, who recorded the arterial blood gas and hemodynamic outcomes, so assessors necessarily knew the intervention status of every patient.
8.location: Pages 2-3, Intervention section; page 3, Results (no blinding statement found in Methods or elsewhere)

9.support: As expected from the severity and from the predicted mortality, only 2 out of 6 patients were alive at 28 days. The direct cause of death in all four patients was sepsis with multiorgan failure.
9.location: Page 4, Results, last paragraph; 28-day outcome recorded for every patient in Table 1, page 3 (no participant lost; baseline and post-intervention data complete for all six)

10.support: We compared all the first values with the second values analysis of variance (ANOVA) with repeated measures. Due to the small sample size and the relatively large number of comparisons, a P value of less than or equal to 0.01 was considered statistically significant.
10.location: Page 3, Statistical analysis (p values printed in Table 3, page 6)

11.support: Respiratory and hemodynamic parameters on baseline and 1 hour after intervention guided by esophageal balloon measurements.
11.location: Table 3, page 6 (a single baseline value compared with a single value one hour after intervention; 24-hour data are only mentioned as 'data not shown', page 4)

12.support: The intervention (esophageal balloon insertion with bedside adjustment of PEEP and inspiratory driving pressure) was applied to individual patients rather than at a group or unit level, so group-level analysis issues do not apply. 'Upon fulfillment of inclusion criteria esophageal balloon was inserted.'

nih.rationale: Rated Fair. The research question is explicitly stated (item 1) and eligibility criteria, including four severity criteria and a list of exclusions, are prespecified and clearly described (item 2); the six consecutive patients are representative of the clinical population of interest, severe ARDS with hypercapnia (item 3), and appear to have been enrolled consecutively (item 4). The intervention is described in enough detail to be reproduced and was applied consistently to all six patients (item 6), the outcome measures are objective and consistently obtained (arterial blood gases, ventilator parameters, PiCCO2 cardiac output; item 7), follow-up was complete with no losses and 28-day status known for all patients (item 9), and paired pre-post statistics with p values are reported (item 10). The rating is pulled down to Fair by three 'No' answers: no sample size justification or power calculation for a six-patient series (item 5, the limitation the authors themselves acknowledge), no blinding of the bedside personnel who titrated ventilation and recorded outcomes (item 8), and outcome measurement at only a single time point before and a single time point after the intervention rather than repeated measures (item 11). The study is also, by design, an uncontrolled before-after case series with no comparator, which limits the ability to attribute the observed changes in PaCO2, tidal volume and cardiac index to esophageal-pressure-guided ventilation rather than to the intervention's timing or other co-interventions.
